info.name: Rental Car Service
info.description:
Covers the full API surface across both rounds: authentication, provider browsing, booking lifecycle, reviews, admin oversight, vehicle fleet, branches, one-way rentals, quotations, delivery, blackout windows, waitlist and claims.

Before running:
1. Start the API and database (`docker compose up -d && uv run alembic upgrade head && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload`)
2. Seed the database (`uv run python -m app.seed`)
3. Run **00 — Setup** first — it logs in as all accounts and discovers every ID the later folders need.

All dates are computed by a collection-level pre-request script and are never hard-coded.

For the expired-claim demo in folder 15: set `CLAIM_WINDOW_MINUTES=1` in `.env` and allow 1 minute to elapse between the offer and the convert attempt.

variable.description: Don Mueang Airport branch under Fast Wheels

exec: // Recomputed before every request so dates never drift.

item.name: 00 — Setup
item.description: Run this folder first. It logs in as all three accounts and discovers the IDs the later folders need. All other folders depend on the variables it sets.

item.name: Discover Providers
item.description: Lists all providers including the retired one (admin only). Stores the four seeded provider IDs for use in later requests.

exec: const ot = providers.find(p => p.name === 'Old Timer Cars');

item.name: Discover Fast Wheels Vehicle Classes
item.description: Lists vehicle classes under Fast Wheels. Stores the first class (Economy) ID.

item.name: Discover Fast Wheels Branches
item.description: Lists branches under Fast Wheels. Stores the Siam branch ID.

item.name: Discover Demo User's Bookings
item.description: Lists the demo user's bookings. Stores the ended booking ID (for the review demo) and the upcoming booking ID (for the negative case: reviewing before period ends).

item.name: Discover Airport Branch
item.description: Finds the Don Mueang Airport branch ID under Fast Wheels.

exec: const airport = branches.find(b => b.name.toLowerCase().includes('airport') || b.name.toLowerCase().includes('don mueang'));

item.name: Discover SUV and Classic Classes
item.description: Finds SUV (full class, waitlist demo) and Classic (unpriced, quotation refusal demo) under Fast Wheels.

item.name: Discover SUV Vehicle
item.description: Finds the single vehicle in the SUV class. Needed for creating a demo blackout window.

item.name: Discover Beta Waitlist Entry
item.description: Retrieves beta's seeded waitlist entry for the SUV class. Needed for the FIFO chain in folder 15.

item.name: Discover Gamma Waitlist Entry
item.description: Retrieves gamma's seeded waitlist entry for the SUV class.

item.name: Discover Alpha's SUV Booking
item.description: Alpha holds the only SUV booking (today+3 to today+10). Needed for the FIFO chain in folder 15.

exec: pm.test('alpha has at least one booking', () => pm.expect(bookings.length).to.be.above(0));

item.name: Register — New Account
item.description: Registers a new user and returns an access token. The body is the full registration shape: name, telephone, email, password.

item.name: Logout
item.description: Logout is client-side. The server invalidates nothing; access tokens are stateless and stay valid until they expire. This is by design, not an oversight — see ADR-0003.

item.name: List Providers — Active Only
item.description: Registered users see only active providers. The retired 'Old Timer Cars' is absent.

item.name: List Providers — Include Retired (Admin)
item.description: Admins may pass include_retired=true to see retired providers in the list.

item.name: Get Provider by ID
item.description: Returns a single provider with its average rating and review count.

exec: pm.test('name is Fast Wheels', () => pm.expect(body.name).to.eql('Fast Wheels'));

item.name: Retire Provider
item.description: Marks the provider as retired. The record is preserved; existing bookings and reviews survive. Retired providers are excluded from the catalogue list.

item.name: 05 — Booking Lifecycle
item.description: A booking requires vehicle_class_id and pickup_branch_id in addition to the dates. A round-one shaped body (dates only) answers 422. The Setup folder discovers these IDs automatically.

item.name: Create Booking
item.description: Creates the demo user's second active booking (the seeded upcoming booking is the first). start_date and end_date are computed by the collection pre-request script.

item.name: Create Second Booking
item.description: Creates the demo user's third active booking. Non-overlapping dates keep both bookings live simultaneously.

item.name: List Bookings (Own)
item.description: A registered user sees only their own bookings. The demo user now holds four: one ended (seeded), one upcoming (seeded), and two just created.

item.name: Re-date Booking
item.description: Replaces the rental period. Provider and vehicle class cannot be changed — extra fields are refused, not ignored.

item.name: 06 — Reviews
item.description: Reviews use the demo user's seeded ended booking. Two rules demonstrated here cannot be shown by an error: an ended booking IS reviewable (201, not 409), and it does NOT count toward the three-booking cap (see folder 08 for the cap test).

item.name: Create Review
item.description: The seeded ended booking is reviewable because its end_date is in the past. Using it here demonstrates that ended bookings transition into the reviewable state.

exec: pm.test('comment updated', () => pm.expect(body.comment).to.eql('Excellent service, would rent again.'));

item.name: Delete Review (Owner)
item.description: The booking's owner may delete their own review. The booking remains and becomes reviewable again.

item.name: List All Bookings (Admin)
item.description: An admin receives every booking in the system, not just their own.

item.name: Create Review (for Admin Delete Demo)
item.description: Re-creates the review on the ended booking so the admin delete can be demonstrated.

item.name: Delete Any Review (Admin)
item.description: An admin may delete any review, not just their own.

item.name: 08 — Negative Cases
item.description: Every guard in the brief, exercised explicitly. Expected status codes are asserted in the test scripts.

item.name: 4th Active Booking — 409 (Cap)
item.description:
The three-active-booking cap. At this point the demo user holds three active bookings: the seeded upcoming booking, booking_id, and booking_id_2. A fourth attempt is refused.

Note: the demo user also holds one ENDED booking. Ended bookings do not count toward the cap — if they did, the limit would have been reached one booking earlier. The 409 here, while the ended booking exists, demonstrates that the cap is applied to active bookings only.

item.name: Reversed Date Range — 422
item.description: end_date before start_date is a malformed request.

item.name: 31-Day Rental — 422
item.description: Rental periods are capped at 30 days inclusive. A 31-day range (tomorrow through in_31) exceeds the cap.

item.name: Past Start Date — 422
item.description: A booking may not start in the past. Re-dating an existing booking may touch past dates, but creation may not.

item.name: Booking Retired Provider — 409
item.description: A retired provider no longer accepts new bookings.

item.name: Review Before Period Ends — 409
item.description: A review may only be written once the rental period has ended. The demo user's seeded upcoming booking ends in the future.

item.name: Second Review — Setup: Create Review
item.description: Creates a review on the ended booking so the duplicate attempt below has something to clash with.

item.name: Second Review on Same Booking — 409
item.description: A booking may only be reviewed once.

item.name: Another User's Booking — 404
item.description: A registered user reaches for a booking belonging to another user. The server answers 404 (not 403) so that booking identifiers cannot be enumerated.

item.name: Cleanup — Delete Review
item.description: Removes the review created for the duplicate-review negative case.

item.name: Cleanup — Delete Booking 1
item.description: Removes booking_id.

item.name: Cleanup — Delete Booking 2
item.description: Removes booking_id_2.

item.name: 09 — Availability
item.description: Shows how GET /providers/{id}/availability reflects both bookings and maintenance blackout windows.

item.name: Get Availability — Clear Range
item.description: Returns free counts for all Fast Wheels vehicle classes on a range with no blackouts. Economy shows 3 free (all vehicles on the road).

item.name: Get Availability — During Economy Blackout Range
item.description: The seeded blackout on Economy vehicle[0] covers today+2 to today+6. Economy shows free_count=2 (not 3) during that range.

item.name: Get Availability — SUV Full (Alpha's Booking)
item.description: Alpha holds the only SUV for today+3 to today+10. free_count=0 for that range.

item.name: 10 — Fleet (Admin)
item.description: Vehicle class and vehicle management. All vehicle routes are admin-only; a plate is fleet administration and of no use to a renter.

item.name: Registered User Cannot Read Vehicles — 403
item.description: Vehicle plates are fleet administration. Registered users are denied even on reads.

item.name: 11 — Branches, Distances & One-Way
item.description: Branch management, delivery radius, inter-branch distances, and one-way rental routes.

exec: const airport = branches.find(b => b.name.toLowerCase().includes('airport') || b.name.toLowerCase().includes('don mueang'));

item.name: Set Delivery Radius on Airport Branch (PUT)
Clear Delivery Radius on Airport Branch (DELETE)
item.description: Clears the radius; existing delivery bookings from that branch are unaffected.

item.name: Get Branch Distance (Siam ↔ Airport)
item.description: The seeded distance between Siam and Don Mueang Airport. Needed before one-way can be enabled.

item.name: List One-Way Routes
item.description: Shows that only Siam → Airport is enabled; Airport → Siam is not.

item.name: One-Way Booking — Siam → Airport (201)
item.description: Creates a one-way Economy booking from Siam to Don Mueang Airport. The response includes a dropoff_branch nested object.

item.name: One-Way Not Enabled — Airport → Siam — 409
item.description: The reverse direction is not enabled in the seed. Airport → Siam is refused with 409.

item.name: 12 — Quotations
item.description: Price estimates without reserving capacity. Shows the rental line, the relocation line for one-way, and the delivery line. The total matches what the booking will charge.

item.name: Quote Round Trip
item.description: Economy, Siam → Siam, 7 days. Returns a rental line only.

item.name: Quote One-Way (with Relocation Line)
item.description: Economy, Siam → Airport. Adds a relocation line: distance_km × relocation_rate_per_km.

item.name: Quote with Delivery (with Delivery Line)
item.description: Economy, Siam, delivery at 5 km (within the 20 km radius). Adds a delivery and collection line.

item.name: Quote One-Way + Delivery (Three Lines)
item.description: All three lines: rental, relocation, delivery.

item.name: Unpriced Class — 409
item.description: Classic has no daily_rate set in the seed. Quotation refuses with 409 rather than quoting zero.

item.name: 13 — Delivery Bookings
item.description: A booking may include a delivery_address and delivery_distance_km. Both or neither; one without the other is 422.

item.name: Create Delivery Booking
item.description: Economy, Siam, delivery at 5 km. The seeded Siam branch radius is 20 km, so 5 km is within range.

item.name: Delivery Beyond Radius — 409
item.description: Siam radius is 20 km. 25 km exceeds it; the response names the radius.

item.name: Branch with No Delivery Radius — 409
item.description: Airport branch has no delivery radius set. Any delivery request from it is refused with 409.

item.name: Missing delivery_distance_km — 422
item.description: Providing delivery_address without delivery_distance_km is refused.

item.name: 14 — Maintenance (Blackout Windows)
item.description: A blackout window takes one vehicle off the road for a period. Only admin may write them; any authenticated user may read them.

item.name: List SUV Blackout Windows — Empty Before Demo
item.description: SUV has no seeded blackout windows. After the next step creates one, the list will have an entry.

item.name: Create Blackout Window on SUV Vehicle
item.description: Schedules a maintenance window on the only SUV vehicle for today+11 to today+12. No booking overlaps that range, so free_count will drop to 0 for those dates.

item.name: Availability During Blackout — SUV free_count=0
item.description: With the maintenance window in place, SUV has 0 free cars for today+11 to today+12.

item.name: Book During Blackout — 409 (Maintenance)
item.description: The only SUV is in the workshop. Booking for those dates is refused naming the maintenance shortfall.

item.name: Overlapping Blackout Window — 409
item.description: Two windows on the same vehicle may not overlap. The second is refused, never merged.

item.name: Registered User Cannot Write Blackout Windows — 403
Update Blackout Window (PUT)
item.description: Replaces the period. Cannot change the vehicle.

item.name: Delete Blackout Window
item.description: The car is back on the road immediately.

item.name: Availability Restored After Blackout Removed
item.description: free_count is back to 1 for today+11 to today+12 now that the window is gone.

item.name: 15 — Waitlist & Claims
item.description:
The seeded state: alpha holds the only SUV booking (today+3 to today+10); beta is position 1 and gamma is position 2 in the SUV waitlist for the same range.

This folder walks the full FIFO chain: full class refusal, joining, alpha cancels, beta gets offered, beta declines, gamma gets offered, gamma converts.

For the expired-claim demo: set CLAIM_WINDOW_MINUTES=1 in .env, wait 1 minute between 'Alpha Cancels' and 'Get Beta Waitlist', then beta's state reads 'expired' and the offer passes to gamma on the next read.

item.name: Try to Book SUV When Full — 409
item.description: Alpha's booking fills the only SUV. Any new booking for that range is refused.

item.name: Join Waitlist When Not Full (Economy) — 409
item.description: Economy has free cars. The waitlist is for when you cannot have the thing; accepting an entry that could be booked immediately would be a worse answer than a sentence.

item.name: Join SUV Waitlist as Fresh User — Position 3
item.description: Beta is position 1, gamma is position 2 from the seed. Fresh joins at position 3.

item.name: Leave Waitlist (Fresh)
item.description: Fresh leaves the queue; the gap closes for those behind. No one else is behind, so positions are unchanged.

item.name: Alpha Cancels SUV Booking — Beta Gets Offered
item.description: Deleting the booking triggers the waitlist. Beta (position 1) gains offered_at and claim_expires_at in the same transaction.

item.name: List Beta’s Waitlist — State: claimed
item.description: Beta now holds a live claim. Converting it books the SUV for the same range.

item.name: Beta Declines Claim
item.description: Declining releases the car immediately rather than holding it until expiry. The offer passes to gamma (position 2) in the same call.

item.name: List Gamma’s Waitlist — State: claimed (Lazy Settle)
item.description: This GET settles the queue for gamma. Beta declined, so gamma is now offered. The settle happens here, not in a background job.

item.name: Gamma Converts Claim — 201 Booking
item.description: Converts the claim into a real booking. The class and dates come from the waitlist entry, not the body. Returns the booking, not the entry.

item.name: Convert Already-Converted Claim — 409
item.description: A claim can only be taken once.

item.name: 16 — Notifications
item.description: Notifications are written by the system, never by the client. The seed creates two for the demo user (one read, one unread) so the surface can be demonstrated before any rule emits one.

item.name: List My Notifications
item.description: Newest first (by created_at then id, both descending). The seed creates one read and one unread notification for demo.

item.name: Mark Already-Read Notification Read — Idempotent
item.description: 200. read_at is unchanged; a retried request must not rewrite when the user first saw this.

item.name: Another User’s Notification — 404
item.description: Notifications are addressed to a person. The fresh user tries to mark the demo user's notification read and gets 404, the same answer as for a notification that does not exist, so ids cannot be enumerated.

exec: pm.test('refused by the ownership check, not a missing route', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.eql('Notification not found.'));
